questions.q: How many distinct practices does 'CI/CD' actually refer to, according to this lesson?
options: Three — Continuous Integration, Continuous Delivery, and Continuous Deployment
One single practice
Two — CI and CD are interchangeable terms for the same thing
Five, one for each day of the work week
questions.explain: CI/CD is actually three chained practices — Continuous Integration, plus either Continuous Delivery or Continuous Deployment, which mean different things despite sharing an abbreviation.

options: Merging code changes back into a shared branch frequently, with an automated build and test on every merge
Deploying code to production without any testing
Writing all code in a single long-lived branch until the project is finished
Manually testing code once a month
questions.explain: CI replaces long-lived diverging branches with frequent merges, each automatically built and tested.

questions.q: What is the key difference between Continuous Delivery and Continuous Deployment?
options: Continuous Delivery requires a human to approve the actual release; Continuous Deployment ships automatically with no approval
They are exactly the same thing with two different names
Continuous Delivery only applies to databases, Continuous Deployment only to applications
Continuous Deployment is slower than Continuous Delivery
questions.explain: Both automate build/test/package, but Delivery stops short of the actual release, requiring a human click; Deployment goes all the way automatically.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does CI mean concretely for a dbt project?
options: Every pull request automatically runs dbt build and dbt test against the changed models before merging
dbt models are manually tested once a year
CI/CD cannot apply to dbt or SQL projects at all
dbt automatically deploys to production with no testing
questions.explain: CI for a dbt project means automated build and test runs on every pull request, catching problems before they reach main.

questions.q: Why might a data team choose Continuous Delivery over Continuous Deployment for an experimental dbt model?
options: To keep a human approval gate before the change reaches the production warehouse, given the higher risk
Because Continuous Delivery is always faster than Continuous Deployment
Because dbt does not support Continuous Deployment at all
There is no reason to ever choose Continuous Delivery
questions.explain: A riskier or experimental change benefits from a human approval step before hitting production, which is exactly what Continuous Delivery provides.
